summary.allegation: The issuer says the cardholder did not authorise the 1,240.50 EUR charge of 1 April 2025 and suggests the card details were compromised.
summary.to_defend: Mastercard requires any two of the listed compelling evidence items showing the genuine cardholder authorised or benefited from the transaction.

requirements.title: AVS and CVV match
requirements.text: AVS match (full address) AND CVV match on the disputed transaction.
requirements.finding: The transaction metadata and the gateway authorisation log both show a full address AVS match (Y) and a CVV match (M) on txn_4412EF.

citations.quote:
AVS check (full address)
Y
Full match

requirements.title: 3DS authenticated
requirements.text: 3D Secure authentication completed successfully (Mastercard SecureCode / Identity Check).
requirements.finding: Mastercard Identity Check authentication completed successfully for txn_4412EF with ECI 02 and an authentication value present, timestamped 2025-04-01 11:08:18 UTC, seconds before authorisation.

citations.quote:
This record certifies that the cardholder was authenticated by their issuing bank under Mastercard
Identity Check (3D Secure 2).

requirements.title: Two prior undisputed transactions
requirements.text: Two prior undisputed transactions from the same cardholder with this merchant in the past 12 months, with matching billing details.
requirements.finding: No transaction history for this cardholder with Velo Continental Rentals was provided; the only supporting hint is a device fingerprint noted as seen three times, which does not identify two prior undisputed transactions with matching billing details.
requirements.gap: No record of two prior undisputed transactions in the past 12 months with matching billing details.

requirements.title: Signed delivery to billing address
requirements.text: Proof of delivery to the cardholder's billing address with signature.
requirements.finding: The merchant is a vehicle rental business (MCC 7512) and the disputed charge is for a rental service, so there are no shipped goods and no signed proof of delivery to provide.

reasons: Every requirement the decision relies on is backed by verified evidence

justification: Two of the four requirements are clearly satisfied, which meets the code's any-two threshold.
rationale:
The issuer alleges the cardholder did not authorise the 1,240.50 EUR charge on txn_4412EF dated 1 April 2025.
The gateway authorisation log shows a full address AVS match (Y) and a CVV match (M) for that transaction ID and amount.
The Mastercard Identity Check record ic_77f31a82bb confirms the issuing bank, BNP Paribas, authenticated the cardholder frictionlessly at 2025-04-01 11:08:18 UTC with ECI 02 and an authentication value present, four seconds before authorisation.
Billing and shipping postcodes match at 75011 and the Paris IP address 90.84.21.117 is consistent with an FR-issued card.
Two of the four compelling evidence requirements are satisfied, meeting the any-two threshold, so the case should be represented.
